name: South Carolina
agency: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources

rule.hpNote: engine of 10 hp or greater, any PWC or specialty propcraft
rule.textEn: Since Aug. 18, 2023, anyone born after July 1, 2007 must pass an approved boater education course before running a boat with 10 hp or more, a PWC or a specialty propcraft.
rule.textEs: Desde el 18 de agosto de 2023, quien nació después del 1 de julio de 2007 debe aprobar un curso de educación náutica antes de manejar una embarcación de 10 hp o más, una moto acuática o una embarcación especial de hélice.

minAge.note: The 2023 law removed the former under-16 operating rule; no separate minimum age is stated.

exemptions: Holders of a USCG vessel operator license or merchant mariner credential (expired ones count).
Non-residents with a certificate or equivalent from another state.
Renters holding a valid boat rental safety certificate.
Accompanied by someone 18+ who is exempt or certified.

card.feeNote: SCDNR's six-hour classroom course is free; online providers charge their own prices. Duplicates for SCDNR/BoatEd courses via ilostmycard.

nonResident: Non-residents with a boating safety certificate or equivalent from their state are exempt.
rental: Renters born after July 1, 2007 can use a boat rental safety certificate (valid 30 days, rental businesses only).
penalty: Civil fine of $50 to $300; not a criminal offense.

sources.publisher: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources
sources.quote: Effective 08/18/2023, Boaters born after July 1, 2007 are required by law to pass an approved boater education course before operating a boat, personal watercraft, or a specialty propcraft powered by 10 hp motor or more.

sources.publisher: South Carolina General Assembly, Code of Laws Title 50 Ch. 21
sources.quote: a vessel powered by an engine of ten horsepower or greater or equivalent to ten horsepower or greater, a personal watercraft, or a specialty propcraft unless the person:

sources.publisher: South Carolina General Assembly, Code of Laws Title 50 Ch. 21
sources.quote: (1) was born on or before July 1, 2007;

sources.publisher: South Carolina General Assembly, Code of Laws Title 50 Ch. 21
sources.quote: is in possession of a license to operate a vessel issued by the United States Coast Guard in the person's name, regardless of the expiration date on the license;

sources.publisher: South Carolina General Assembly, Code of Laws Title 50 Ch. 21
sources.quote: is a nonresident in possession of a boating safety certificate, or an equivalency, issued by another state in the nonresident's name;

sources.publisher: South Carolina General Assembly, Code of Laws Title 50 Ch. 21
sources.quote: is accompanied by a person at least eighteen years old who meets one of the criteria in items (1) through (5) of this subsection.

sources.publisher: South Carolina General Assembly, Code of Laws Title 50 Ch. 21
sources.quote: must be fined not less than fifty dollars and not more than three hundred dollars

sources.publisher: South Carolina General Assembly, Code of Laws Title 50 Ch. 21
sources.quote: A violation of this section does not constitute a criminal offense

sources.publisher: South Carolina General Assembly, Code of Laws Title 50 Ch. 21
sources.quote: deleted (9), which related to persons younger than sixteen years of age operating a personal watercraft, specialty propcraft, or vessel

sources.publisher: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources
sources.quote: The boat rental safety certificate is valid for 30 days from the date of issuance

sources.publisher: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources
sources.quote: This six-hour, one-day class provides hands-on learning

sources.publisher: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources
sources.quote: SCDNR accepts any National Association of Safe Boating Law Administrators approved course (NASBLA).
